missing_information_behavior: Do not infer vitamin C deficiency from a single low fruit/vegetable response; clarify food sources, fortified foods and existing supplements.
safety_exclusions: Do not claim vitamin C supplements prevent common colds or replace dietary improvement.
Do not recommend high-dose vitamin C without indication and safety review.
Do not ignore kidney-stone or iron-overload context.
professional_escalation_conditions: Scurvy-like symptoms, malabsorption, smoking, kidney stones, chronic kidney disease or hemochromatosis.
population_and_context: People reporting low fruit and vegetable intake; vitamin C intake may warrant dietary review, but intake should be assessed across all foods and fortified products.
dose_constraints: No dose from this rule. Assess dietary intake against life-stage reference values and reconcile supplemental exposure.
certainty_and_limitations: NIH ODS Vitamin C fact sheet describes food sources, reference values and high-dose risks; dietary pattern alone does not diagnose deficiency.
